TourSkipBody: You will start in No privileges, which needs no administrator approval. You can change the run mode, or watch this tour again, in Settings › Run mode.
TourWelcomeBody: Connect your computers, servers and phones into one private network. First, a minute on a few things that shape everyday use.
TourWelcomeNote: About a minute. You can skip it, and watch it again in Settings › Run mode.
TourDeviceBody: With a virtual device, an EasyTier network is like another network adapter in this computer: any app reaches the other devices' virtual addresses, with nothing to set up.
TourDeviceAppsYes: Browsers, remote desktop, SSH and games on this computer reach the other devices' virtual addresses.
TourDeviceNeedsHelper: Needs the privileged helper, installed once with administrator approval.
TourDeviceAppsNo: Other apps on this computer cannot open connections to the devices in the network.
TourDeviceInboundNo: Other devices still reach this computer by its virtual address, and through it the local network it shares as a subnet.
TourModesBody: They differ in whether there is a virtual device and in what runs the networks. Pick one to start; you can switch any time in Settings.
TourModeUserNote: Good for a first try, or when other devices only need to reach this computer.
TourModeFollowNote: Good for everyday use: open the app when you need it, quit it when you don't.
TourModeBackgroundNote: Good for a NAS or a small box that must stay online, perhaps with nobody signed in.
TourArtUserCaption: Networks run in the app, with no virtual device
TourArtFollowCaption: Networks run in the helper, while the app is open
TourArtBackgroundCaption: Networks run in the helper, from startup
TourStartupSvcTitle: Online from startup, no sign-in needed
TourStartupSvcBody: The background service starts with the system: once the computer starts, networks connect even at the sign-in screen with nobody signed in, and they keep running when you quit the app. Good for a box in the corner, or a computer you reach remotely before signing in.
TourStartupAppBody: In {mode}, networks run with the app. With the switch below on, they connect once the computer starts and you sign in to your account; at the sign-in screen this computer is offline.
TourLoginSvc: Only the window and the tray icon; networks run either way.
TourLoginOn: Starts in the tray after you sign in, and connects.
TourLoginOff: Connects only once you open the app yourself.
TourUseBackgroundAsk: Need it online without signing in?
TourArtAlwaysCaption: Online from startup, no sign-in needed
TourArtAfterSignInCaption: Online only after you sign in
TourArtAfterOpenCaption: Online only after you open the app
TourAwakeTitle: To stay online, keep the computer awake
TourAwakeBody: While the computer sleeps or hibernates it is offline in every run mode, and the other devices cannot reach it. For a computer that should stay online:
TourAwakeWin1: Settings › System › Power & battery › Screen, sleep & hibernate timeouts: set sleep when plugged in to Never.
TourAwakeWin2: Closing a laptop's lid puts it to sleep; change that under “Lid, power & sleep button controls”.
TourAwakeMac1: System Settings › Battery › Options: turn on “Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off”. On a desktop Mac, it is under Energy.
TourAwakeMac2: Closing a MacBook's lid puts it to sleep unless it has power and an external display.
TourAwakeLinux1: Turn off automatic suspend in your desktop's power settings.
TourAwakeLinux2: Closing a laptop's lid suspends it; change the lid action in the same settings.
TourAwakeScreen: Turning off only the display keeps it online.
TourArtScreenOK: The display may turn off; sleep takes it offline

TourReadyAuthMac: When you finish, macOS asks once for an administrator password to install the privileged helper. Opening the app never asks again.
TourReadyAuthLinux: When you finish, the system asks once for authorization to install the privileged helper. Opening the app never asks again.
